:::{#thm-cauchy-schwarz}
#### Cauchy-Schwarz inequality

For any $\vecf{x}, \vecf{y} \in \reals^p$,

$$
\abs{\vecf{x} \cdot \vecf{y}} \le \norm{\vecf{x}}\,\norm{\vecf{y}},
$$

with equality exactly when $\vecf{x}$ and $\vecf{y}$ are linearly dependent
(@def-linearly-independent).

:::

::: proof

**If $\vecf{y} = \vzero$.**
Then $\vecf{x} \cdot \vzero = \sum_i x_i \cd 0 = 0$ (@def-dot-product)
and $\norm{\vzero} = 0$ (@thm-norm-properties, part 1),
so both sides are $0$ and equality holds;
and $\vecf{x}, \vecf{y}$ are linearly dependent, because $0\,\vecf{x} + 1\,\vecf{y} = \vzero$.

**If $\vecf{y} \ne \vzero$.**
Then $\norm{\vecf{y}} > 0$ (@thm-norm-properties, part 1).
Let $t \eqdef (\vecf{x} \cdot \vecf{y}) / \norm{\vecf{y}}^2$. Then

$$
\ba
\norm{\vecf{x} - t\,\vecf{y}}^2
&= \norm{\vecf{x} + (-t)\,\vecf{y}}^2
&& \text{(subtraction is adding } -1 \text{ times)}
\\
&= \norm{\vecf{x}}^2 + 2\,\paren{\vecf{x} \cdot ((-t)\,\vecf{y})} + \norm{(-t)\,\vecf{y}}^2
&& \text{(@thm-norm-sum-square)}
\\
&= \norm{\vecf{x}}^2 + 2\,(-t)\,(\vecf{x} \cdot \vecf{y}) + \norm{(-t)\,\vecf{y}}^2
&& \text{(@thm-dot-linear, special case } b = 0 \text{)}
\\
&= \norm{\vecf{x}}^2 + 2\,(-t)\,(\vecf{x} \cdot \vecf{y}) + \paren{\abs{-t}\,\norm{\vecf{y}}}^2
&& \text{(@thm-norm-properties, part 2)}
\\
&= \norm{\vecf{x}}^2 - 2t\,(\vecf{x} \cdot \vecf{y}) + t^2\,\norm{\vecf{y}}^2
&& \text{(} 2\,(-t) = -2t \text{ and } \abs{-t}^2 = t^2 \text{)}
\\
&= \norm{\vecf{x}}^2 - 2\,\frac{(\vecf{x} \cdot \vecf{y})^2}{\norm{\vecf{y}}^2}
 + \frac{(\vecf{x} \cdot \vecf{y})^2}{\norm{\vecf{y}}^4}\,\norm{\vecf{y}}^2
&& \text{(substitute } t \text{)}
\\
&= \norm{\vecf{x}}^2 - 2\,\frac{(\vecf{x} \cdot \vecf{y})^2}{\norm{\vecf{y}}^2}
 + \frac{(\vecf{x} \cdot \vecf{y})^2}{\norm{\vecf{y}}^2}
&& \text{(cancel one factor } \norm{\vecf{y}}^2 \text{)}
\\
&= \norm{\vecf{x}}^2 - \frac{(\vecf{x} \cdot \vecf{y})^2}{\norm{\vecf{y}}^2}.
&& \text{(combine the last two terms)}
\ea
$$ {#eq-cauchy-schwarz-chain}

The left side is at least $0$ (@thm-norm-properties, part 1), so

$$
\ba
0
&\le \norm{\vecf{x}}^2 - \frac{(\vecf{x} \cdot \vecf{y})^2}{\norm{\vecf{y}}^2}
&& \text{(@eq-cauchy-schwarz-chain)}
\\
\frac{(\vecf{x} \cdot \vecf{y})^2}{\norm{\vecf{y}}^2}
&\le \norm{\vecf{x}}^2
&& \text{(add } (\vecf{x} \cdot \vecf{y})^2 / \norm{\vecf{y}}^2 \text{ to both sides)}
\\
(\vecf{x} \cdot \vecf{y})^2
&\le \norm{\vecf{x}}^2\,\norm{\vecf{y}}^2,
&& \text{(multiply both sides by } \norm{\vecf{y}}^2 > 0 \text{)}
\ea
$$

and taking nonnegative square roots of both sides,
which preserves the inequality,
gives $\abs{\vecf{x} \cdot \vecf{y}} \le \norm{\vecf{x}}\,\norm{\vecf{y}}$.

**When equality holds ($\vecf{y} \ne \vzero$).**
Both sides of the inequality are nonnegative,
so equality holds exactly when
$(\vecf{x} \cdot \vecf{y})^2 = \norm{\vecf{x}}^2\,\norm{\vecf{y}}^2$,
that is (dividing by $\norm{\vecf{y}}^2 > 0$ and rearranging),
when $\norm{\vecf{x}}^2 - (\vecf{x} \cdot \vecf{y})^2 / \norm{\vecf{y}}^2 = 0$.
By @eq-cauchy-schwarz-chain, that quantity is $\norm{\vecf{x} - t\,\vecf{y}}^2$,
so equality holds exactly when $\vecf{x} - t\,\vecf{y} = \vzero$
(@thm-norm-properties, part 1),
that is, when $\vecf{x} = t\,\vecf{y}$.

- If $\vecf{x} = t\,\vecf{y}$, then $1\,\vecf{x} + (-t)\,\vecf{y} = \vzero$,
  so the two vectors are linearly dependent.
- Conversely, suppose $a\,\vecf{x} + b\,\vecf{y} = \vzero$ with $a, b$ not both $0$.
  Then $a \ne 0$:
  otherwise $b \ne 0$ and $b\,\vecf{y} = \vzero$,
  so $\vecf{y} = \tfrac{1}{b}\,(b\,\vecf{y}) = \vzero$, contrary to assumption.
  Subtracting $b\,\vecf{y}$ from both sides gives $a\,\vecf{x} = -b\,\vecf{y}$,
  and multiplying by $\tfrac{1}{a}$ gives $\vecf{x} = s\,\vecf{y}$ with $s = -b/a$. Then

  $$
  \ba
  \abs{\vecf{x} \cdot \vecf{y}}
  &= \abs{(s\,\vecf{y}) \cdot \vecf{y}}
  && \text{(substitute } \vecf{x} = s\,\vecf{y} \text{)}
  \\
  &= \abs{s\,(\vecf{y} \cdot \vecf{y})}
  && \text{(@thm-dot-linear, special case } b = 0 \text{, first slot)}
  \\
  &= \abs{s}\,\abs{\vecf{y} \cdot \vecf{y}}
  && \text{(} \abs{ab} = \abs{a}\,\abs{b} \text{)}
  \\
  &= \abs{s}\,\norm{\vecf{y}}^2
  && \text{(} \vecf{y} \cdot \vecf{y} = \norm{\vecf{y}}^2 \ge 0 \text{, @eq-l2-norm)}
  \\
  &= \paren{\abs{s}\,\norm{\vecf{y}}}\,\norm{\vecf{y}}
  && \text{(regroup)}
  \\
  &= \norm{\vecf{x}}\,\norm{\vecf{y}},
  && \text{(@thm-norm-properties, part 2)}
  \ea
  $$

  so equality holds.

:::

{{< slidebreak >}}

:::{#exm-cauchy-schwarz}
#### A strict case and an equality case

- For $\vecf{x} = (1, 2)$ and $\vecf{y} = (3, 4)$:
  $\vecf{x} \cdot \vecf{y} = 3 + 8 = 11$,
  while $\norm{\vecf{x}}\,\norm{\vecf{y}} = \sqrt{5} \cd 5 \approx 11.18$.
  The inequality is strict, and the vectors are linearly independent:
  $(3, 4)$ is not a multiple of $(1, 2)$, since $3 \cd 2 \ne 4$.
- For $\vecf{x} = (1, 2)$ and $\vecf{y} = (2, 4) = 2\,\vecf{x}$:
  $\vecf{x} \cdot \vecf{y} = 2 + 8 = 10$
  and $\norm{\vecf{x}}\,\norm{\vecf{y}} = \sqrt{5}\,\sqrt{20} = \sqrt{100} = 10$,
  so equality holds.

:::
